Nothing in the package is built yet: one `main()` that prints a greeting, and two smoke tests. So this is a New-Project Entry.

I'm treating `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md` as your words, because it's your brief. The three research files are background. Lines that come only from a research file are marked as candidates for you to confirm.

One caveat on the cost notes: I've read only the opening 3,000 characters of each research file. The ChatGPT file's §3.3 data-availability inventory would firm up several estimates. It's a cheap read, and I'll do it before writing the roadmap.

## Outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome | Source | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Revision series for each of the four stages (1st→2nd, 2nd→3rd, 3rd→benchmark, post-benchmark/wedge-back) for total nonfarm, SA, from real vintages | brief | Small. All PAYEMS vintages should come from one ALFRED request. The FRED API limit is 120 requests/min. |
| O2 | Revision scale over time by stage (rolling dispersion and tails), total nonfarm | brief | Negligible compute once O1 exists. |
| O3 | Same revision series for NSA, so SA and NSA vintages line up | brief | Depends on whether NSA vintages are in ALFRED. Unknown until checked. |
| O4 | Supersector revision series, SA and NSA | brief | About 25 series (≈12 supersectors × SA/NSA). ALFRED's vintage depth at supersector level is unknown, and that is the main data risk. |
| O5 | Decomposition of SA revisions into an NSA-sample part and a seasonal-factor part, by stage | brief | Cheap compute. It needs O3, and O4 for the sector view. |
| O6 | Collection-interval covariates (days from the reference period to release, closing rates) and their relation to 1- and 2-month revision scale | brief | Days can be computed from release dates. Closing rates are hand-built from BLS tables, and how far back they go is unknown. |
| O7 | Hand-built annual covariates: real BLS appropriations, CRs, shutdowns, sequestration, FTE, sample size and design events | brief; "hand-built" from research files | Your time. About 40 fiscal years of budget justifications plus FedScope. I can't estimate the per-year effort without trying one. |
| O8 | An honest statement of which capacity effects (funding, staffing, sample) are identified from about 40 years of data, and which aren't | brief | Measured by the stage that runs it. |
| O9 | A multi-vintage state-space model of total nonfarm: a latent path, stage-specific news and noise, Student-t errors, covariates on log-scale with SV | brief | Only a real NUTS run can tell. The core stage measures it. |
| O10 | The benchmark as an irregular, higher-precision observation, with wedge-back as an observation operator | brief | Limited because BLS doesn't archive QCEW vintages (brief). Compute is measured by the stage that runs it. |
| O11 | Partial pooling of driver effects across supersectors | brief | Needs O4. Compute scales with sector count, measured by the stage that runs it. |
| O12 | Validation: PPCs on dispersion, LOO against a constant-variance baseline, pseudo-real-time checks, MCMC diagnostics | brief | Pseudo-real-time means refitting many times. That cost is a multiple of O9's measured fit time. |

## Proposed tracks

- **A — Vintage data and descriptive scale (O1–O4).** Known progression, *if* you can name its stages. My guess is total nonfarm SA, then NSA, then supersectors. Every other track consumes it.
- **B — Seasonal vs. sample decomposition (O5).** Research. Split from C and D because the decomposition stands without any covariate answer.
- **C — Collection interval and short-horizon scale (O6).** Research. Split from D because it is identified off within-year variation, while D's covariates are slow-moving and trending. Each answer stands alone, and joined, C would wait on D's hand-building.
- **D — Institutional capacity (O7, O8).** Research. It is the most labor-intensive track and the most weakly identified.
- **E — Full multi-vintage Bayesian model (O9–O12).** Research. Split because the news/noise question across stages stands without B–D. C and D don't need to wait for E's machinery to give a first answer.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 with uv, pytest and ruff (from the repo).
- NumPyro (NUTS), Dynamax, Blackjax only if warranted, ArviZ, and Polars for the vintage panel (from the brief).
- The estimand is the scale of revisions, with covariates entering the variance, not only the mean (from the brief).

## Proposed name

`ces-revisions`, so the roadmap would be `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`.

## Optional probe

I can fetch all vintages of PAYEMS and of one supersector series from ALFRED, SA and NSA. That would confirm vintage depth and supersector coverage, which is the biggest unknown behind O3 and O4. It needs a FRED API key, and I'll run it only on your yes.

## What I need from you

Please rank the outcomes within each track and rank the tracks against each other. Also confirm or change the tracks, their kinds and the name, including Track A's stage sequence if it is a known progression. Then say yes or no to the probe.
